content: Tinidazole has been associated with neurological adverse reactions, including convulsive seizures and peripheral neuropathy. Peripheral neuropathy is primarily characterized by symptoms such as numbness or paresthesia in an extremity. If any abnormal neurological signs appear during treatment, it is imperative to discontinue tinidazole therapy immediately. The use of tinidazole may lead to the development of vaginal candidiasis, with Candida vaginitis reported in approximately 7% of study subjects. Tinidazole should be administered with caution in patients who have a history of or current evidence of blood dyscrasia, as this condition may predispose them to complications. Prescribing tinidazole (Tindamax) in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection, or without a valid prophylactic indication, is unlikely to benefit the patient. Moreover, such inappropriate use increases the risk of promoting the development of drug-resistant bacteria.
